title: A gate failure that is the host's is a host fault, not a verdict on the work: not counted, judged again, and two in a row halt for a human
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the module comment (step 4 and the halt rules), `judge_pushed()` (the `rejected` closure and the verdicts), `halt_reason()` and `HALT_AFTER`, `no_room()` and `aborted()`; `Verdict.output` and `decide()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/gate.rs (what the gate printed, stdout then stderr marked `! `); in scripts/rsi/gate.sh the regression section (`| == regression: <check> must still pass`, the reason `regression: <check> fails on the candidate`) and rsi/scenarios/check-tests.sh (it prints `grep -E 'FAILED|panicked|^error' -A5 | head -n 40` of `cargo test --quiet --workspace`: each failing test's `thread '<name>' panicked at <file>:<line>:<col>:` with its message, and `test result: FAILED. ...`); you may not edit them; the errors the `postgres` crate gives a test (its Display, `db error: ...`, and its Debug, `Error { kind: Db, cause: Some(DbError { ... code: SqlState(E57P02) ... }) }`) in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/common/; `spawn_integrator_record` (the verdicts it accepts) and the `task.gated` case of `spawn_control_apply` (`gate_rejections`, `gate_aborts`, the `gate_room_*` fold) in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; the stall layer's `halted` step (dispatch/stall.rs); web/src/components/rsi/Verdicts.tsx and web/src/missionTimeline.ts; docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 and docs/design.md §14. Objective 018 (the resource checks before a gate) is the companion of this one; this one stands alone (it does not need 018 to be solved first).

The problem. A gate that fails because the host failed is recorded as a verdict on the work. On 2026-11-06 the test PostgreSQL crashed mid-gate (its 64 MB /dev/shm: "could not resize shared memory segment", then a segfault and a restart); every database test failed at once with a connection error, and the integrator recorded `rejected` ("regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate"): it counted toward the mission's three-rejections halt, the worker got the failures as its own mistake, and the same candidate would have passed on a healthy host. The evidence that it was the host is in what the gate printed and in the test database's own log; nothing reads it.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. When it applies. The gate rejects the candidate with the reason `regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate`. The failures are read from the gate's output: the check-tests section (from the line `| == regression: check-tests.sh must still pass` to the next `| == ` or `| stage gate ` line); a failure is a `| thread '<test>' panicked at <location>:` line with its message (the `| `-prefixed lines after it up to a line starting `| note:`, `| ---- `, `| test result:`, `| --` or a blank one), or an `| Error: ...` line of a test that returned an error. Any other rejection reason is judged as today.
2. A failure is the host's when its message holds one of: `error connecting to server`, `Connection refused`, `connection closed`, `server closed the connection unexpectedly`, `terminating connection because of crash of another server process`, `the database system is in recovery mode`, `the database system is starting up`, `the database system is shutting down`, `the database system is not yet accepting connections`, `could not resize shared memory segment`, `SqlState(E57P0`, `SqlState(E080` (a connection error to the test database); or, when the test database's log shows a crash in the gate's window (3), when its message is a database error of any kind (holds `db error` or `Error { kind: Db`). Any other failure (an assertion, a panic of the code under test, a timeout) is the work's.
3. The test database's log. SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_LOG (new, optional) names a file the integrator can read: the test server's log, lines as PostgreSQL writes them with `log_line_prefix` `%m [%p] ` (`2026-11-06 01:46:58.017 UTC [1] LOG:  ...`; a numeric offset instead of `UTC` is read too). It shows a crash in the gate's window when a line holding `was terminated by signal`, `terminating any other active server processes` or `all server processes terminated; reinitializing` is stamped within [the gate's start - 1 s, the gate's end + 1 s], both measured by the integrator around the gate process. Unset or unreadable: no log evidence (said once in the integrator's output).
4. The verdict. When at least one failure was read and every failure read is the host's, the integrator records `host_fault`, not `rejected`. A real failure among them keeps it `rejected`, as today. `host_fault` is not a verdict on the work: the task stays where it was (`reported`, or `accepted` under review), its `revisions` and `review_note` do not move, nothing goes back to the worker, and neither `gate_rejections` nor `gate_aborts` moves (the rejection and abort runs neither grow nor reset). The record names, besides `base`, `candidate`, `revision`, `scenarios`, `reason` (`host fault: ...`, saying which evidence) and `log` (the gate's output): `evidence` (`failures` when every failure is a connection error, else `server_log`), `failures` (one entry per failure read: `test`, `message` (its first line, bounded), `class` (`connection` or `database`)), `crash` (the log lines that showed the crash, when used), `host_faults` (the count in a row, this one included) and `escalate`.
5. Judged again. The next pass judges the task again with no wait of its own (with objective 018 solved, its checks run first, so a host still short of room gives `no_room`, not another gate).
6. Two in a row halt. The mission's host faults in a row are folded by the store (a new `gate_host_faults` column, folded in `spawn_control_apply`: + 1 on `host_fault`, unchanged on `no_room` and `stale`, 0 on every other verdict and on `mission.resumed`). The `host_fault` that makes it 2 carries `escalate` true, and the mission halts (`halt_reason`, at the next pass at the latest) with a reason naming `2 host faults in a row` and the last one's reason: the gate is not run again until a human resumes, the stall layer's `halted` step and the board show it. The halt rule for rejections (three in a row) is unchanged and never counts a host fault.
7. Every reader of verdicts knows `host_fault`: `spawn_integrator_record` accepts it; `DELIVERY_TASKS` and the objective history treat it like `no_room` (no step change); the RSI and Missions pages show it as its own verdict (the host's, not the work's) in web/src; the supervisor's digest names it when it lists verdicts.
8. Causality (§14): the decision rests on the gate's recorded output (each failure and its message, named in the record) and on the test server's log lines stamped inside the gate's measured window, both named in the record; not on the reason's text alone, and not on time.
State the rule in the module comment of integrate.rs (step 4, beside "No room is not a verdict"), in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 (the verdicts and the halt rules) and in docs/storage.md if it lists verdicts. Add unit tests in integrate.rs: the failure parser on real check-tests output (one failure, several binaries, a truncated list, an `Error:` line); every connection pattern; a real failure among connection errors stays `rejected`; database errors with a crash in the window are `host_fault`, with one outside it are `rejected`; the log's timestamps with `UTC` and with an offset; the halt after two in a row, not after one; a host fault between two rejections leaves the rejection run as it was. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: `spawn_integrator_record` accepts `host_fault`, and the fold of `gate_host_faults` and of the task.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/020.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge, no supervisor) runs four residents of one gated mission on a fake engine; `spawn integrate --once` passes, run by the scenario with SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_LOG set (and objective 018's thresholds met), judge through a recording gate that prints check-tests.sh's failure lines as scripts/rsi/gate.sh does and rejects with `regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate`, by what the candidate holds: hostA (three connection errors), mixed (two connection errors and an assertion), olddb (database errors that are not connection errors; the log's only crash is an hour old), hostB (two connection errors, then database errors while the gate appends a segfault and a restart to the log). It checks:
- (1) hostA: `host_fault`, gate_rejections and gate_aborts unchanged, the task `reported` with its revisions unchanged, no halt; `evidence` `failures`, `failures` naming the three tests, `host_faults` 1;
- (2) the host fixed, the next pass judges hostA again, accepted, and it lands;
- (3) mixed: `rejected`, gate_rejections + 1;
- (4) olddb: `rejected`, gate_rejections + 1;
- (5) hostB: `host_fault` (`host_faults` 1), then `host_fault` by the log (`evidence` `server_log`, `crash` holding `was terminated by signal 11`, `host_faults` 2, `escalate` true), then the mission halts with a reason naming the host faults and the gate does not run on hostB again.
On the live main (06cc205; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "(1) task #1, whose every check-tests failure is a connection error to the test database, was gated 'rejected' (regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate), not 'host_fault'; gate_rejections 0 -> 1". It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
